newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Landfill waste proposal adoption delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Landfill waste proposal adoption delayed again.

text.p: Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard's plans for Commission adoption of a revised draft directive for rules governing landfill waste dumps have been delayed once again, a Commission spokesman said on Friday.
"The proposal has been delayed because it will need some further internal discussions in the Commission. It will be on the agenda the week after next," the spokesman told Reuters.

The proposal is intended to replace the draft COM(93)275 thrown out by the European Parliament in May last year when deputies were unable to get assurances from the Commission that it would support their amendments.
Euro-MPs had wanted to remove a proposed derogation from the landfill rules exempting small islands and sparsely populated regions.

The replacement proposal has run into problems in recent weeks first with Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, because of planned limits on the organic content of landfill waste, and recently due to reservations, expressed by Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis, about limits on small-island derogations.
The dossier is likely to require further discussions in a special chefs-de-cabinet meeting before it gets an airing in Commission.
